title: Big Ideas in Tech for 2023: An a16z Omnibus
edition_framing: Each idea is what a16z partners expect builders to tackle in 2023.

entries.label: Breakthroughs in buying (finally!)
entries.quote: Social commerce, discovery commerce, video commerce—these trends are inevitable, and 2023 will be the year it all becomes obvious.
entries.subject: Social and video commerce
entries.author: Connie Chan

entries.label: Labor marketplaces become specialized
entries.quote: It’s likely that in 2023, a new wave of labor marketplaces will help employees build identity and reputation, connect directly with hiring managers, and get training and resources to build their careers.
entries.subject: Specialized labor marketplaces
entries.author: Olivia Moore

entries.label: Mainstream AI adoption: More *fun* than you think
entries.quote: In 2023, AI-focused founders will put user behaviors and psychology first to create products that can be readily embraced by everyday consumers.
entries.subject: Consumer AI applications
entries.author: Bryan Kim

entries.label: Unlocking the “third place”
entries.quote: What are the next generation of tools and platforms that are built to serve consumers, community builders, and creators in the post-Covid, hybrid world?
entries.subject: Online third places (community platforms)
entries.author: Anne Lee Skates
entries.note: The idea is stated only as a question.

entries.label: Tech reveals new sources of inventory
entries.quote: In 2023, I think we’ll see a wave of companies that enable sellers to tap into alternative sources of inventory.
entries.subject: Alternative inventory sources for sellers
entries.author: Justine Moore

entries.label: Craigslist, dismembered and reinvented
entries.quote: But a few ripe categories remain to be ripped, including blue-collar jobs, home services, and rentals.
entries.subject: Unbundling of online classifieds
entries.author: Jeff Jordan

entries.label: B2C gets B2B distribution
entries.quote: As management teams ramp up in the coming year, we expect consumer companies to pursue B2B partnerships to drive non-inflationary distribution, avoiding the typical Facebook, Instagram, Google, and Apple “taxes.”
entries.subject: B2B distribution for consumer companies
entries.author: Alex Immerman and Jamie Sullivan

entries.label: Precision delivery of medicines
entries.quote: In 2023 we hope to finally see a breakthrough in precision delivery that will unleash a landslide of queued-up therapeutic approaches to progress into the clinic.
entries.subject: Precision drug delivery
entries.author: Vineeta Agarwala and Becky Pferdehirt

entries.label: Chemical-induced proximity
entries.quote: We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of proximity-inducing chemistry and in 2023 we expect continued breakthroughs in the field.
entries.subject: Chemical-induced proximity (drug modality)
entries.author: Vineeta Agarwala and Ben Portney

entries.label: The modern bio software stack
entries.quote: The industry’s appetite for science-native software-as-a-service tools is accelerating.
entries.subject: Bio software and tools stack
entries.author: Jorge Conde and Jay Rughani

entries.label: The biggest company in the world
entries.quote: We expect consumer healthcare to be front and center in 2023.
entries.subject: Consumer healthcare
entries.author: Vijay Pande and Daisy Wolf

entries.label: The value-based care stack
entries.quote: VBC done right demands purpose-built approaches that will be built on a fundamentally different stack.
entries.subject: Value-based care technology stack
entries.author: Julie Yoo and Justin Larkin

entries.label: Compliance as a competitive advantage
entries.quote: In 2023, companies of all sizes will turn to software to solve their challenges.
entries.subject: Compliance software
entries.author: Angela Strange and Joe Schmidt

entries.label: Tools for stretching your dollar
entries.quote: While we’ve seen significant focus and investment over the past 5+ years on innovating around the front-end of financial transactions, we’ll see a market shift in 2023 toward building tools to better manage the often unseen (yet vital) back-office functions of running a healthy financial services business.
entries.subject: Financial back-office software
entries.author: David Haber

entries.label: GPT unlocks credit counseling
entries.quote: We expect to see this capability—and services like it—become available for subprime and early-credit consumers in particular.
entries.subject: AI credit counseling
entries.author: Anish Acharya

entries.label: The infrastructure stack for business banking
entries.quote: In 2023, we expect to see more companies tackling the infrastructure layers needed to bring business banking into the digital age (at most banks, the business owner is still required to show up in person just to open an account!).
entries.subject: Business banking infrastructure
entries.author: Angela Strange and Marc Andrusko

entries.label: The race for “know-your-everything”
entries.quote: In 2023, both new founders and existing startups will continue to vie for the most coveted spot within fintech infrastructure: the one-stop-shop for identity verification and onboarding.
entries.subject: Identity verification and onboarding (KYC)
entries.author: Seema Amble and Marc Andrusko

entries.label: Fintechs are becoming banks
entries.quote: In 2023, we expect more digitally native lenders to pursue bank charters.
entries.subject: Fintech bank charters
entries.author: Alex Immerman and Justin Kahl

entries.label: Payment infrastructure opportunity in Latin America
entries.quote: Hence, I see an opportunity for a white-label payment processor in Latin America.
entries.subject: White-label payment processing in Latin America
entries.author: Gabriel Vasquez

entries.label: Embracing large language models while maintaining trust
entries.quote: In 2023, fintech companies will need to strike a delicate balance between pushing the envelope by building with new technology rails such as large language models (LLMs), but also maintaining customer trust.
entries.subject: Large language models in financial services
entries.author: Sumeet Singh

entries.label: FedNow may be just the beginning
entries.quote: It will incentivize third-party infrastructure built on top of payment rails, as has been the case across the world.
entries.subject: FedNow real-time payments
entries.author: Santiago Rodriguez
entries.note: FedNow is the Federal Reserve's real-time payment network; it launched in July 2023.

entries.label: Web3 games persist—and thrive
entries.quote: We’re on the cusp of unlocking a new generation of web3 native games that will be fun, broadly appealing, and uniquely enabled by blockchain technologies.
entries.subject: Web3 games
entries.author: Jonathan Lai

entries.label: Production-ready generative AI for every type of game asset
entries.quote: The biggest revolution to hit gaming in 2023 will be the creation of production-ready generative AI models for all asset types needed to produce a modern game.
entries.subject: Generative AI for game assets
entries.author: James Gwertzman

entries.label: Entertainment franchise games will explode
entries.quote: In fact, I expect they’ll become even more popular in 2023.
entries.subject: Entertainment franchise games
entries.author: Andrew Lee

entries.label: Games developed on mobile, for mobile
entries.quote: I believe we’ll see more mobile-first game creation.
entries.subject: Mobile-first game development
entries.author: Troy Kirwin

entries.label: Games as theater
entries.quote: As the concept of the metaverse evolves, I hope that developers in 2023 will shift back to this idea of launching games that focus on creative tools, features, and infrastructure as an integral part of their games’ core loop.
entries.subject: Games with creative tools (user creation)
entries.author: Lester Chen

entries.label: Games supplant social networks
entries.quote: In 2023, I expect games to take the reins from social networks in new and meaningful ways.
entries.subject: Games as social networks
entries.author: Joshua Lu

entries.label: Games as a neverending Turing test
entries.quote: In the year ahead, you may not know who’s who anymore—and you won’t mind.
entries.subject: AI agents in games
entries.author: Jack Soslow

entries.label: AI native games
entries.quote: We’ll see emergent, procedurally generated worlds, each populated with their own rich histories, inhabitants, and mysteries.
entries.subject: AI-native games
entries.author: Justin Paine

entries.label: Web3 games redefine fun
entries.quote: In the year ahead, developers will pinpoint what makes their games intrinsically fun—and why web3 is a necessary component.
entries.subject: Web3 games
entries.author: Robin Guo

entries.label: The Metaverse goes fashion forward
entries.quote: Brands that lean in, like Gucci, will be rewarded by the hearts and wallets (both physical and digital) of consumers.
entries.subject: Digital fashion in virtual worlds
entries.author: Doug McCracken

entries.label: Overhauling the space supply chain
entries.quote: In 2023, the Space Industrial Base will continue to grow in size, birthing critical companies serving our nation’s interests.
entries.subject: Space industrial base
entries.author: Ryan McEntush

entries.label: Small modular reactors advance the nuclear renaissance
entries.quote: While there is still a way to go in reforming the regulatory frameworks for these types of reactors, SMRs and the broader nuclear industry are likely poised for growth in the year ahead.
entries.subject: Small modular nuclear reactors
entries.author: Michelle Volz

entries.label: Industrial robotics scale vertically
entries.quote: We’re likely to see robotics companies develop automation solutions for specific verticals, and scale to service multiple use cases within these industries, rather than performing a particular task across sectors.
entries.subject: Vertical industrial robotics
entries.author: Oliver Hsu

entries.label: Reshore and restore: Bringing everything back home
entries.quote: After decades of sending everything offshore, we’re bringing everything back home.
entries.subject: Reshoring of supply chains
entries.author: Grant Gregory

entries.label: The industrial economy goes digital
entries.quote: I believe we’ll see even more innovation enabling the digitization of our industrial economy in the upcoming year.
entries.subject: Digitization of industrial economy
entries.author: Kimberly Tan

entries.label: Generative AI advances beyond “text to image” to complex workflows
entries.quote: In 2022, much of this took the form of AI-generated images of dogs flying in outer space or AI avatars reflecting the best version of our self(ies), but in 2023 and beyond, the enterprise productivity implications will start to shine.
entries.subject: Generative AI for enterprise workflows
entries.author: Sarah Wang

entries.label: Strength in value-based sales
entries.quote: As budgets tighten, software investments will come under increased scrutiny.
entries.subject: Value-based enterprise software sales
entries.author: Joe Morrissey

entries.label: The next generation of SaaS applications
entries.quote: In the coming year, I expect we’ll see a new generation of SaaS platforms emerge to meet those heightened expectations for how software should work.
entries.subject: Next-generation SaaS applications
entries.author: Zeya Yang

entries.label: Blockchain’s mobile moment
entries.quote: But more people are now starting to care about decentralizing access to blockchains for all users—even those who cannot run a node themselves.
entries.subject: Blockchain light clients (mobile)
entries.author: Noah Citron

entries.label: Zero knowledge, multi-party computation, and post-quantum crypto
entries.quote: It would be fantastic to see more constructions for zk-proofs that fill the gaps in the multidimensional space of these tradeoffs.
entries.subject: Zero-knowledge proofs, multi-party computation and post-quantum cryptography
entries.author: Valeria Nikolaenko
entries.note: A research wish list rather than a forecast.

entries.label: Developer onboarding for zero knowledge
entries.quote: I expect these developments, along with continued theoretical advances, will lead to an influx of application developers, given how significant zero knowledge is to so many use cases.
entries.subject: Zero-knowledge developer tooling
entries.author: Michael Zhu

entries.label: VDF hardware
entries.quote: I’m excited for the first generation of VDF hardware to be available, paving the way for practical deployment.
entries.subject: Verifiable delay function (VDF) hardware
entries.author: Joseph Bonneau

entries.label: Fully on-chain games and autonomous worlds
entries.quote: We are at the very beginning of crypto-native, fully “on-chain games,” or—as others prefer to call its superset—“autonomous worlds,” built on top of blockchain technology.
entries.subject: Fully on-chain games (autonomous worlds)
entries.author: Carra Wu

entries.label: Non-transferable tokens
entries.quote: I’m excited to see the various web3 applications that will be built on top of not just this primitive, but also with decentralized identifiers and verifiable credentials.
entries.subject: Non-transferable tokens (soulbound tokens)
entries.author: Michael Blau

entries.label: Decentralized energy
entries.quote: I’m excited to see builders continue to expand what’s possible in this category of decentralized energy coordinated by blockchains.
entries.subject: Decentralized energy on blockchains
entries.author: Guy Wuollet
